subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: For invalid local avatars, should direct `/avatar/{agentId}` remain a generic 404 while authenticated metadata/UI surfaces show safe reasons, or should the raw endpoint expose reason-specific errors such as 413 for oversized files?
rationale: The remaining fix crosses the local file-serving diagnostic boundary; automation can patch webchat fallback behavior, but it should not choose how much raw endpoint information to disclose.

options.title: Keep raw 404 and improve UI metadata
options.body: Preserve the conservative file-serving boundary and make webchat/settings suppress broken images and show safe metadata-based diagnostics.

options.title: Expose selected raw errors
options.body: Allow specific direct-endpoint statuses such as 413 for oversized avatars, with security review and tests proving no sensitive path or existence information leaks.

options.title: Defer diagnostics
options.body: Accept the current generic 404 behavior and leave clearer oversized-avatar recovery to a later UX-focused issue.

recommendation.title: Keep raw 404 and improve UI metadata
recommendation.body: Preserve the conservative file-serving boundary and make webchat/settings suppress broken images and show safe metadata-based diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and hardened the avatar resolver and Control UI file-serving boundary most directly involved in this decision.
